# Beyond Correctness: Resolving Underspecification in Agentic Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#planpool)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.02739v1) · arXiv:2610.02739v1, 2 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 22 pages: Sections 1-7, AI/reproducibility statements, Appendices A-D, Algorithms 1-2, case-study SQL, tables and complete method-specific prompts.

## Research question

Agents can identify useful clarification questions yet silently abandon them before generating SQL, producing apparently correct but weakly grounded answers.

## Method

Stores a ranked question pool outside conversational context, permits explicit additions/removals, routes questions through a pool tool, and blocks final submission while items remain. The generator, datasource tools and simulated-user backbone are held fixed across strategy variants.

## Evaluation

171 BIRD-Lite and 225 BIRD-Full cases are selected because the same agent succeeds with all clarifications supplied; 297 Spider cases contain injected ambiguities. Claude-Opus-4.8 plays agent and simulator. Metrics distinguish execution, annotated-ambiguity coverage and cost.

## What the results support

Pool enforcement improves annotated recall and grounded success over prompt-only planning while asking more questions. It does not maximize execution accuracy: on BIRD-Full, self-reflection scores 70.7% versus 67.1% for PlanPool.

## Limits and qualifications

Groundedness counts an ambiguity as addressed when a simulator maps a question to it, rather than verifying faithful incorporation of the answer. Solvability filtering conditions results on the chosen model; tool action costs are removed. Explicit dropping and incomplete initial plans prevent any guarantee that all real ambiguities are resolved.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A concrete persistent clarification-state mechanism with conditional simulator evidence and a distinct accounting-versus-resolution boundary.
